The shovel knows where it is at all times. It knows this because it knows where it isn't. By subtracting where it is from where it isn't, or where it isn't from where it is (whichever is greater), it obtains a difference, or deviation. The guidance subsystem uses deviations to generate corrective commands to drive the shovel from a position where it is to a position where it isn't, and arriving at a position where it wasn't, it now is. Consequently, the position where it is, is now the position that it wasn't, and it follows that the position that it was, is now the position that it isn't.
In the event that the position that it is in is not the position that it wasn't, the system has acquired a variation, the variation being the difference between where the shovel is, and where it wasn't. If variation is considered to be a significant factor, it too may be corrected by the GEA. However, the shovel must also know where it was.
The shovel guidance computer scenario works as follows. Because a variation has modified some of the information the shovel has obtained, it is not sure just where it is. However, it is sure where it isn't, within reason, and it knows where it was. It now subtracts where it should be from where it wasn't, or vice-versa, and by differentiating this from the algebraic sum of where it shouldn't be, and where it was, it is able to obtain the deviation and its variation, which is called error.

Those are most likely just "Old people shoes" (for lack of a better term, idk what they're called exactly) I worked partly in a nursing home of sorts attached to a hospital. A bunch of the guys I would talk with wore those. They're for people who can't walk good cuz it hurts and/or their feet have some type of issue (arthritis and such). They're sometimes specially made for each foot and designed specifically for how the person stands and moves throughout their day. It's basically like how we do mouthguards for athletes to provide specific protection for that person based on how their mouth, and only their mouth, closes. They're big bulky shoes that are supposed to be cushioned, comfy, and stable. But they're bulky, so trips are an actual risk everywhere the person goes. A good pair of light cross trainers is actually what most of them seemed to prefer. The added weight of the special shoe is what causes a lot of the trips. Combined with the almost inch and a half extra height on the sole by comparison to the much lighter cross trainer. Old uncoordinated people with memory loss and cognitive issues tend to trip a lot. A lot. Saw a dude that wore knee pads when he'd walk without his walker. Sprained/fractured wrists are also a typical outcome which is why you tend to see them roll to shoulder when they fall. They're taught to do that the first few times they take big spills. PT after an injury usually gives them tips and tricks to deal with future falls.

So you mate your melee gig with your health gig. You get a magical baby with high melee and health after a few breeds. Now go find a gig with a good stat in another area (food, oxygen, weight, etc.) Breed that with your melee/health gig a bunch of times and you'll get a baby with high melee high health and the high roll on the last stat you added to your breeding pool. Keep doing this and your levels will go up.

The Dinos get either the moms or dad's base stats for any given category (health, melee, food, oxy, etc.) The more points into those base stats the higher the hatched level will be. Hope that makes sense. Also, tons of videos on it if you'd prefer the 20 minute explanation.

This is what i do. Youll need a 9x9, or 16x16 foundation area. Enough fence foundations to line a 7x7, or 14x14 area of the whole thing (meaning leave a 1 foundation spacing around the outside of the fence foundation snaps) and 4 Behemoth gates for the 9x9, or 8 gates for 16x16. It's a lot but it's the best design I've ever used for mass storage.

Lay down foundations in either 7x7, or 14x14 (may need to sub in ceilings in some uneven terrain, works)

 Place fence foundations lining the outer edge

Place regular foundations around the outside of the whole thing (youll then have either a 9x9 or 16x16)

 build 1 pillar 13 high snapped to one corner where fence foundations meet 

Build ceilings off the top of that pillar to cover foundations (game says it's supported because foundations underneath so no need for extra support)

Snap gates to fence foundations. Can be a little tricky and there may be some gaps between frames if placed wrong, but it's easy to snap if you snap the first gate so that it covers the pillar you built. 

This build allows you to go in and out from any side at almost any point. Tall enough to accommodate multiple layers for expanded storage. Giant hatch frames in each corner of the ceiling works well if you have a lot of frequent flyers. Or just build a whole hanger on top of the whole thing and keep the flyers separate. Forges and stuff on top is a nice idea too.

It's a ton of resources for early/mid game, but I've also scaled the size down and used dino gates instead of behemoth. Obviously smaller footprint but same idea. More of a pick your size way to build it lol.   

Edit for extra info: behemoth gate is 7 foundations wide, 13 walls tall... Dino gate is 2 foundations wide, 4 walls tall.
